$comment: OMN-18414. THE ONE GRAMMAR FOR THE `Gate:` KEY.
A `Gate:` line in a Linear issue description is read by two independent
mechanisms. The AUTHORING authority is omniclaude's ticket-creation
admission guard, which refuses a create whose binding line it cannot
read. The READING consumer is omnibase_infra's evidence autoclose sweep,
which resolves the line to decide whether a Done-flip candidate names a
live surface that has to be green first.
Before this contract the two carried DISJOINT vocabularies. The guard
mandated four forms and the closer accepted exactly one form that was not
among them, so every ticket the guard admitted was a typed hold at the
closer, and the form the closer required would have been refused at
creation. Four Done-candidates were held on nothing else at the
2026-09-15T21:34Z dry-run tick.
This file is the single declaration. Neither consumer carries a private
form regex; each compiles the patterns below and matches them in order.
WHY THIS IS DATA READ TWICE RATHER THAN ONE IMPORTED MODULE. The guard's
decision core imports only the standard library. Its hook script resolves
an interpreter that may be a bare system python3 and runs it with
`env -u PYTHONPATH`, so importing a packaged module would turn a missing
dependency into a refusal of every Linear write on the machine. The guard
already records that constraint for the OMN-18135 proof-class vocabulary,
which it transcribes with its source revision pinned for the same reason.
This contract follows that established construction: one canonical
declaration here, a transcription on the guard side, and a drift test that
fails when the two diverge.
WHY TWO LINE PATTERNS AND ONE FORM LIST. The asymmetry between the two
line patterns is deliberate and is NOT the defect this contract closes.
At AUTHORING time a bulleted binding line is refused, because a bullet is
how a line ends up inside a checklist that binds nothing. At READING time
the closer faces descriptions already written, including quoted and
emphasised ones, so it tolerates leading quote, bullet and emphasis
characters and the `Gate probe:` spelling. The language the reading
pattern accepts is a strict superset of the authoring one, which is what
`line_pattern_superset_fixtures` pins. What must NOT differ, and what did,
is `forms` -- the grammar of the binding VALUE.
WHY EXACTLY ONE FORM IS A PROBE. `probe` says what a form resolves to.
Only `workflow_run` is a proof pointer: it names a workflow file whose
newest completed run's conclusion is the ticket's own declared evidence,
and anything but `success` holds the flip. That is the OMN-16106
behaviour, unchanged. The other four forms are TRACEABILITY bindings --
they say which commitment a ticket exists to serve -- and resolving them
to a live probe is refuted rather than merely unimplemented:
* A release-criterion or invariant id cannot resolve to the beta board's
live cell, because the board is generated FROM Linear. Its own module
states it re-reads `Linear and every probe against GitHub on each run`
(omninode_infra tools/beta_board/beta_board_data.py:4, :760, :1981).
Holding a Linear state flip on a cell derived from that ticket's Linear
state is a cycle, and a cycle resolves to whatever it was seeded with.
* A live-gate-defect check name cannot resolve to a check run. The name
is a BROKEN SURFACE, named because it is broken, so it is red by
construction at filing time and green only once the ticket's own work
lands. It is frequently not a CI context at all: OMN-18403's
`workspace-reconcile-status` matches no check run on omnibase_infra's
dev HEAD and appears in no workflow in either repository, against a
positive control on the same endpoint that returns check-run names.
A form declaring `probe: none` therefore reaches the stage after the probe
on its own. It is NOT a pass on the ticket -- every other conjunct of the
sweep still applies -- it is the absence of a proof pointer, stated.
There is deliberately NO wildcard form and no escape value. A binding line
matching no form below is a typed hold naming these forms, never a silent
pass and never a reported red conclusion: a sanctioned spelling for an
unreadable binding is a sanctioned incident.
CASE-INSENSITIVITY IS INLINE `(?i)`, NOT A FLAGS ARGUMENT. A consumer
compiling these with `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE` trips omnibase_infra's
union-usage ratchet, which counts the `|` as a type union. The inline flag
is equivalent, and raising a ratchet ceiling to get past a false positive
is how ceilings stop meaning anything.

normalizations.$comment: Linear rewrites a plain `OMN-16990` typed into a description as an issue-mention element, so the text a reader gets back is not the text the author wrote. A parent-criterion pattern built against the authored spelling matches nothing on any live ticket. Replaced with the identifier the element wraps.
A binding an editor has auto-linked reads as `[OMN-16990](url)`. The link target is never part of a binding, so the visible text is kept and the target dropped.
A binding written inside a code span is the same binding. Backticks are stripped after the other rewrites so a mention nested in a span is still reached.
Applied last so `OMN-16990   AC-1` and a newline-wrapped equivalent are one binding.

forms.$comment: `Gate: OmniNode-ai/omnibase_infra chain-canary.yml`. The only proof pointer. A bare filename is deliberately NOT accepted: defaulting the repository to whichever one the companion happens to live in resolves a DIFFERENT workflow of the same name and reports its colour as this ticket's proof, which is worse than declining to answer.

`Gate: C9`. Shape only; membership is checked by the authoring guard against the release-criterion ids it pins from the beta PRD. The reading consumer does not re-check membership -- an id the PRD has since dropped is a stale binding on an already-created ticket, not a reason to withhold a Done-flip.
`Gate: INV-103`. Zero-padded to at least three digits because that is the invariant registry's own spelling, so `INV-12` is a typo for `INV-012` and is refused rather than guessed at.
`Gate: OMN-16729 AC-5`. Both halves are required: a bare parent is a link, not a binding.

`Gate: live-gate defect: kb-doc-gate`. The check must actually be named. This is the one form that also exempts a residual-shaped title at the authoring guard, because a defect in a live gate is not a residual of anything.

rejected.$comment: a bare workflow filename is ambiguous across repositories
a repository with no workflow file names no run
a bare parent is a link, not a binding
the broken check is not named
an empty binding line binds nothing
